newsitem.title: USA: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Cisco vols drop, options active.
newsitem.headline: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Cisco vols drop, options active.

text.p: Implied volatilities in Cisco Systems Inc options fell Wednesday amid heavy options activity after the company reported largely in-line fiscal fourth quarter earnings late Tuesday, traders said.
Cisco ended down 1-9/16 at 80-3/8 on heavy volume of about 15.6 million shares. It reached a session low of 79-1/8.
The networking company said it earned pro forma earnings of $0.55 a share against $0.42 a share last year.
The earnings met published Wall Street estimates, but fell short of the so-called "whisper" number, which some traders said was as high as $0.60 per share.
Patrick Hamilton at LETCO in Chicago said volatility in most Cisco options had dropped to the low 40 percent area from the mid-50's on Tuesday.
"There's been a lot of sellers of September premium, specifically the September 85s," he said.
The Cisco September 85 calls traded 5,330 contracts and finished down 1-3/8 at 2-7/8. Open interest through Tuesday, when 1,634 contracts were added, was 3,620.
Hamilton also said investors were buying both the August 80 calls and puts, which traded roughly 7,530 and 6,960 contracts, respectively.
The August 80 call fell 2-1/8 to 2-1/8 and the put slipped 3/16 to 1-5/8.
Options activity was steady through the September and October series and a few January calls drew solid interest.
Hamilton said it appeared investors were either buying calls or selling puts "to get long the stock," with a focus on the September series.
"In September we've had some big sellers of volatility," he said. "August is pretty much over as far as what's going to happen."
August options expire at the end of next week and Hamilton said he expected the stock would likely trade around the 80 strike price at least until then.
"It seems the stock has a difficult time moving away from the 80 strike," he said.
